html:
The African infantry of the French colonial army, founded by Faidherbe in Senegal in 1857 and later recruited from across French West and Central Africa.

They did most of the fighting in France's conquest of Africa. In the First World War some 200,000 served, and about 30,000 died, many at Verdun and on the Somme; Blaise Diagne led the recruiting drive of 1918. They fought again in 1940 and 1944, and then in Indochina and Algeria. Their pensions were frozen at independence and only fully restored decades later. The Thiaroye massacre is the darkest page of their story.
sum: The African infantry of the French colonial army, founded by Faidherbe in Senegal in 1857 and later recruited from across French West and Central Africa.
